LESSON: WESTERN MUSICAL INSTRUMENTS (SOLO PERFORMER)

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: MUSIC AND DANCE FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Performing
Topic 2.4: Western Musical Instruments (Solo Performer)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Western Musical Instruments (Solo Performer), part of Performing in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 MUSIC AND DANCE FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: Why do instruments sound differently while playing the same pitch?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Western Musical Instruments (Solo Performer) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Citizenship: The learner gains skills in playing a solo musical instrument from the rest of the world (western)

gaining international awareness.

● Digital Literacy: The learner downloads; watches and listens to professional musicians perform Western

instruments.

● Self-Efficacy: The learner confidently executes playing techniques that are specific to the selected Western solo

instrument.

Values:
● Integrity: The learner uses the internet appropriately when searching for music pieces to play.

● Responsibility: The learner uses instruments and digital devices with appropriate assistive technology learning

resources with utmost care.

● Respect: The learner respects others’ views during rehearsal sessions of the western instrument.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Online safety: The learner responsibly sources for instrumental music to play from the internet.

● Life skills: The learner acquires music reading skills that will help in interpreting scored music.

Suggested Learning Resources

● Western Solo musical instrument.

● Resource persons.

● Braille equipment and materials.

● Exercise books in appropriate print.

● ICT devices with appropriate assistive technology.

● Internet connectivity.

43

Suggested Key Skill to be Assessed

● Describing the structure of the western solo instrument.

● Explaining the tuning of a selected Western solo musical instrument.

● Playing a selected Western solo musical instrument applying playing techniques.

● Playing a selected Western solo musical instrument observing performance directions.
